inline_prompts: You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_N) of length N, consisting of 0 and 1. We call a string S of length N, a good string if it is possible to perform the following operation any number of times (possibly zero) Here, S_i (1\leq i\leq N) denotes the i-th character of S, and we define S_{N+1}=S_1, S_{N+2}=S_2, and A_{N+1}=A_1. - Perform one of the following operations: - Choose an integer i with 1\leq i\leq N such that S_i= A, S_{i+1}= R, and S_{i+2}= C, and replace each of A_i and A_{i+1} with the value 1. - Choose an integer i with 1\leq i\leq N such that S_{i+2}= A, S_{i+1}= R, and S_i= C, and replace each of A_i and A_{i+1} with 1. Determine whether there exists a good string. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output If there exists a good string, print Yes; otherwise, print No. The judge is case-insensitive; for example, if the correct answer is Yes, outputs such as yes, YES, or yEs will also be accepted. Constraints - 3\leq N\leq 200000 - A_i\in \lbrace 0,1 \rbrace (1\leq i\leq N) - All input values are integers.
